sources.title: Allen Hatcher, Algebraic Topology, Chapter 2
sources.locator: Degree pp.134–137; Lemma 2.34 pp.137–139; Axioms for Homology pp.160–162 up to Categories and Functors; exercises 1–4 p.165; §2C Theorem 2C.1 and Lemma 2C.2 pp.177–179; Theorem 2C.5 pp.182–184. These are disjoint read ranges, not a claim to have read every intervening section.

contents.name: Degree
contents.support: Definition uses H_n(S^n)=Z and excludes n=0.

contents.name: Degree properties (a), (e), (f)
contents.support: Identity, orientation reversal and composition of n+1 reflections determine the signs.

contents.name: Degree property (b)
contents.support: Omitted-point factorization through a contractible sphere complement.

contents.name: Degree properties (c), (d), forward implications
contents.support: Homotopy invariance, composition and homotopy-equivalence signs; the converse is harvested separately.

contents.name: Degree property (g)
contents.support: Fixed-point-free maps deform to antipodal by normalized straight lines.

contents.name: Theorem 2.28
contents.support: Both the normalized-field obstruction and explicit complex rotation were read.

contents.name: Proposition 2.29
contents.support: The degree character of a free action on a positive even sphere is injective into {+1,-1}.

contents.name: Local degree (unnumbered definition preceding Proposition 2.30)
contents.support: Read the relative-group/excision diagram and its local generators.

contents.name: Proposition 2.30
contents.support: Read the full diagram chase: diagonal class, local components, sum.

contents.name: Example 2.31
contents.support: Pinch and fold with local signs; signed two-disk variation carries the degree-zero counterexample.

contents.name: Example 2.32
contents.support: Local angular stretching and rotation show each positive power contribution has sign +1.

contents.name: Proposition 2.33
contents.support: Cone-pair boundary/suspension square is natural.

contents.name: Axioms for Homology
contents.support: Read reduced homotopy, exactness and wedge axioms; pair translation and dimension discussion.

contents.name: Reduced/unreduced translation (unnumbered)
contents.support: Kernel augmentation and quotient pairs, with separate treatment of an empty subspace.

contents.name: Uniqueness with coefficient group G (unnumbered assertion)
contents.support: The text points ahead to 4.59. That proof has been dependency-audited; finite simplicial comparison supplies the earlier route.

contents.name: Mayer–Vietoris from the axioms (unnumbered)
contents.support: Read the relative identification and diagram mechanism before the next section heading.

contents.name: Exercise 2
contents.support: Use the precise product-of-graded-homology modulo direct-sum functor, with degree reindexing for boundaries; do not substitute a vague continuity failure.

contents.name: Simplicial Approximation; Theorem 2C.1
contents.support: Read star-cover/Lebesgue/mesh construction and complete straight-line homotopy. The finite-pair adaptation is explicit in the manifest.

contents.name: Simplicial Approximations to CW Complexes; Theorem 2C.5
contents.support: Read M(f), C(f), common Z_n and both deformation retractions, including endpoint correction by HEP. Build the finite-pair specialization here.

contents.name: Degree property (c), Hopf converse (forward reference to Corollary 4.25)
contents.reason: Equality of degree classifies sphere homotopy classes only after later homotopy-theoretic inputs; this design explicitly reserves that converse for AT-12.

contents.name: Lemma 2.34, singular homology vanishing and skeletal stabilization
contents.support: Existing singular result is reused only in its singular scope; it is not a continuity axiom for arbitrary h.

contents.name: Lemma 2.34, mapping telescope alternative proof
contents.support: The locally stationary infinite deformation, not just compact singular chains, supplies a homotopy equivalence usable by arbitrary theories.

contents.name: Extraordinary theories, shifted homology, and bordism discussion
contents.reason: Dropping dimension and constructing bordism or general graded coefficient theories belongs to generalized homology; this page proves ordinary uniqueness. The specific nonadditive zero-coefficient example needed to test ordinary uniqueness is separately included.

contents.name: Exercise 1
contents.reason: The torsion subgroup and torsion-free quotient failures of exactness are different counterexamples from the required infinite-additivity obstruction; they do not supply a missing step in this page.

contents.name: Exercise 3
contents.support: Derive suspension from the reduced axioms, rather than adding it as an independent axiom.

contents.name: Exercise 4
contents.support: Finite wedge additivity is weaker than the arbitrary wedge assertion used in the telescope proof.

contents.name: Lemma 2C.2
contents.support: Nonempty intersection of open stars characterizes vertices spanning a simplex.

contents.name: Simplicial mapping cylinder M(f) and mapping cone C(f) construction in proof of 2C.5
contents.support: Both constructions, their finite triangulations and relative endpoint control will be proved within the model lemma; ordinary mapping cylinders of simplicial maps are not silently assumed to be simplicial.

contents.name: Theorem 2C.5, countable and arbitrary CW refinements
contents.reason: Only the finite-pair version is needed to construct the comparison. Infinite CW homology is handled by an explicit telescope, so no general infinite simplicial-model theorem is required here.

contents.name: Local degree after suspension (unnumbered consequence of 2.33)
contents.support: Note that suspending a degree-d map gives an isolated pole with local degree d in dimension at least two; it is a direct consequence, not a new item.

contents.name: Proposition 2.30 and Example 2.32, local power-map calculation
contents.support: Apply the local-degree sum after factoring a polynomial by repeated division. A straight-line homotopy of its nonvanishing factor to a constant reduces the local group map to an angular power map. This avoids importing an analytic normal form from outside the declared prerequisites.

sources.read_evidence: Full 88-page chapter PDF fetched and the listed complete arguments read through web. Page references are printed pages; PDF page 37 is printed 134. Full-book table of contents independently checked in AT%2B.pdf.

sources.title: J. Peter May, A Concise Course in Algebraic Topology
sources.locator: Contents; Ch.14§3 suspension corollaries p.109; 14§4 pp.110–111; 14§5 opening triple/excisive-sum/Mayer–Vietoris statements pp.112–113; all of 14§6 pp.114–116; all of 15§2 pp.119–120 (not problems pp.121–122).

contents.name: Corollaries: suspension isomorphism and homology of spheres
contents.support: Sphere groups follow from coefficient G by iterated natural suspension; connecting maps are compatible with the cofiber construction.

contents.name: 4. Reduced homology theories; Definition for nondegenerately based spaces
contents.support: Specialize the source definition to based CW spaces and retain the published empty-space convention.

contents.name: Theorem: equivalence of theories on based spaces and pairs of spaces
contents.reason: The full all-space comparison uses a weak-equivalence axiom and CW approximation outside the assigned category. The later theorem in this same section for CW pairs is included instead; no CW result is removed.

contents.name: Corollary: splitting off the basepoint summand
contents.support: Basepoint section splits augmentation for a nonempty based space.

contents.name: Definition: reduced homology theory on based CW complexes; Theorem: equivalence with CW-pair theories
contents.support: Exact quotient pairs and wedge additivity correspond; the basepoint must be a vertex.

contents.name: 5. The Mayer–Vietoris sequence; long exact sequence of a triple (unnumbered)
contents.support: Triple exactness is needed for successive skeletal boundaries.

contents.name: Lemma: excisive relative direct-sum isomorphism
contents.support: The relative excision identification is the input to the natural exact-sequence diagram.

contents.name: Theorem: Mayer–Vietoris exact sequence
contents.support: The source leaves the diagram chase to the reader; Miller Lemma 11.6 supplies its explicit algebraic form.

contents.name: 6. Passage to colimits; Theorem: homology commutes with sequential colimits of inclusions
contents.support: Read the complete telescope proof, not only the statement. On CW skeleta replace the source weak-equivalence step with Hatcher direct deformation.

contents.name: Lemma: direct-sum presentation of the colimit
contents.support: 1-shift is injective and its cokernel is the colimit; maps need not be injective.

contents.name: Mapping telescope definition and odd/even decomposition in theorem proof
contents.support: Its cover turns Mayer–Vietoris into the algebraic direct-sum presentation.

contents.name: Homotopy colimits (closing remark)
contents.reason: The remark points toward arbitrary diagram-shaped homotopy colimits. This page needs only the sequential telescope of CW skeleta and does not construct a general homotopy-colimit theory.

contents.name: 2. The uniqueness of the homology of CW complexes; definition of C_n(X), d
contents.support: Relative skeletal groups and successive boundary maps form a chain complex before identifying its incidence matrix.

contents.name: Theorem: C_*(X) is isomorphic to the cellular chain complex of X
contents.support: The source proof uses Hurewicz. Our supplied finite simplicial comparison and sphere-endomorphism lemma replace that later input; the matrix claim itself is preserved.

contents.name: Arbitrary coefficients C_*(X;pi)=C_*(X) tensor pi (unnumbered paragraph)
contents.support: Coefficients are arbitrary abelian groups; no flatness or tensoring of an already-computed homology group is asserted.

contents.name: Theorem: natural cellular computation compatible with connecting homomorphisms
contents.support: The full three-skeleton exact diagram constructs alpha(x) as the class of rho(y). Finite-dimensional stabilization is proved first; the infinite step is separately supported by 14§6.

sources.read_evidence: Full 251-page PDF fetched. Read complete colimit/telescope proof and complete cellular uniqueness proof including the exact diagram. Contents identify Ch.13 Axiomatic and cellular homology, Ch.14 Derivations of properties, Ch.15 Hurewicz and uniqueness.

sources.title: Allen Hatcher, Algebraic Topology, author revised complete edition
sources.locator: Contents pp.iii–v; Ch.0 Propositions 0.16–0.19 and Corollaries 0.20–0.21, pp.15–17 with full proof of 0.19; Theorem 3F.8 pp.314–315, statement and complete proof.

contents.name: Proposition 0.16
contents.support: CW prism retractions and weak-topology continuity provide HEP; use the published statement.

contents.name: Proposition 0.17
contents.support: Contraction of a contractible cofibration subspace extends and descends to the quotient; this justifies cone-versus-quotient identifications.

contents.name: Proposition 0.18; Proposition 0.19; Corollary 0.20
contents.support: Read the relative attachment proof and all three stages of the relative homotopy-inverse proof, including the retracing cancellation.

contents.name: Corollary 0.21
contents.support: The common mapping-cylinder space has both ends as deformation retracts when its map is a homotopy equivalence.

contents.name: Theorem 3F.8, homology assertion and proof
contents.support: Independent telescope/Mayer–Vietoris proof of direct-limit homology; it explicitly cites the direct deformation in 2.34.

contents.name: Theorem 3F.8, cohomology assertion
contents.reason: The inverse-limit and lim-one cohomology sequence concerns contravariant theories and is not a prerequisite for covariant ordinary homology uniqueness. No cohomology colimit claim is made here.

sources.recovery: The original full-book URL returned a web cache/fetch failure. Recovered the author full revised AT%2B.pdf, fetched 560 pages and read these exact passages. Chapter citations otherwise remain at their directly fetched chapter URLs.
sources.read_evidence: Contents and named results read in the recovered text; no harvest is attributed to the failed full-book URL.

sources.title: Allen Hatcher, Algebraic Topology, Chapter 4
sources.locator: Theorem 4.59, homology statement and proof, pp.399–401, stopping before the cohomology proof.

contents.name: Theorem 4.59, homology uniqueness
contents.support: The conclusion backs the assigned theorem. Its degree-action argument uses pi_n(S^n)=Z; the present scaffold supplies a finite-polyhedral replacement and does not assume this later result.

contents.name: Use of sphere homotopy classification in the proof of 4.59
contents.reason: The design reserves classification of sphere maps for AT-12. The needed integer action on arbitrary coefficients is proved here by simplex chains and subdivision, so the later homotopy classification is not load-bearing.

sources.read_evidence: Full 84-page PDF fetched; the homology proof was read to identify its use of sphere-map classification and cellular approximation.

sources.title: Haynes Miller, MIT 18.905 Algebraic Topology I, Lecture 10
sources.locator: All mathematical content of the five-page lecture PDF: opening Proposition 9.6 and §10 Excision and applications, Definitions/Theorems/Corollaries 10.1–10.8, printed pp.22–25.

contents.name: Proposition 9.6
contents.support: Two-out-of-three for already existing maps of pair LES, not existence of a theory morphism.

contents.name: 10. Excision and applications; Definition 10.1
contents.support: Record the closure/interior excisive-triple condition faithfully; do not omit the closure because of PDF text extraction.

contents.name: Theorem 10.2
contents.support: Excision statement; its proof is deferred in this lecture and already published locally.

contents.name: Corollary 10.3
contents.support: Read the excision/two-out-of-three quotient proof.

contents.name: Proposition 10.4
contents.support: Sphere groups and disk relative groups; augmented S^-1 convention in this source is not imported into empty reduced homology.

contents.name: Corollary 10.5
contents.support: Distinct sphere dimensions have distinct reduced homology support.

contents.name: Corollary 10.6
contents.support: Puncture corresponding points and retract radially.

contents.name: Theorem 10.7
contents.support: Read the no-retraction and ray-continuity proof; the manifest includes an explicit formula to discharge continuity.

contents.name: Theorem 10.8
contents.support: Existence/surjective degree monoid map; the source also notes classification belongs later.

sources.read_evidence: Read full lecture-set contents and every mathematical paragraph of lecture 10, including the ray argument and the degree construction; source printed pagination is pp.22–25, not a guessed chapter locator.

sources.title: Haynes Miller, MIT 18.905 Algebraic Topology I, Lecture 11
sources.locator: All mathematical content of the six-page lecture PDF: §11 Eilenberg–Steenrod axioms and locality, Definition 11.1 through Lemma 11.6 and its proof, printed pp.25–28.

contents.name: 11. The Eilenberg–Steenrod axioms and the locality principle; Definition 11.1
contents.support: Exactness, excision, homotopy, dimension, and Milnor arbitrary disjoint-sum additivity; singular verification is given immediately.

contents.name: Definitions 11.2 and 11.3
contents.support: Interior covers and cover-small singular simplices explain the already-published locality proof being packaged, not a new small-chain theory.

contents.name: Theorem 11.4 (Locality principle)
contents.support: Published chain-homotopy equivalence gives the stronger form of the stated homology isomorphism.

contents.name: Excision from locality (unnumbered derivation)
contents.support: Read the small-chain quotient identification, not only the source citation.

contents.name: Theorem 11.5 (Mayer–Vietoris)
contents.support: The local goal extends the singular statement to every axiomatic theory using the relative excision diagram.

contents.name: Lemma 11.6
contents.support: Every third vertical isomorphism in a map of exact sequences gives the interleaved Mayer–Vietoris sequence; include the actual element chase.

sources.read_evidence: Full PDF fetched; read axiom verification, small-simplex definitions, locality statement, excision derivation, Mayer–Vietoris and Lemma 11.6 proof.

sources.title: Jiří Lebl, Guide to Cultivating Complex Analysis
sources.locator: §1.3 stereographic construction and Exercises 1.3.1–1.3.9, pp.19–20; Lemma 5.1.1 and Definition 5.1.2, pp.122–123; Theorem 5.1.3 p.123 read as a stronger comparison, not used.

contents.name: Theorem 5.1.3
contents.support: Published stronger analytic normal form was read during dependency audit. The example does not depend on it because that page is outside the allowed prerequisite closure; elementary polynomial division and a nonvanishing-factor homotopy prove every needed local-degree assertion inline.

contents.name: Exercise 1.3.9
contents.support: The leading-term lower bound proves P(z) tends to infinity and hence extends continuously to the sphere.

contents.name: Stereographic projection (unnumbered construction)
contents.support: The explicit inverse stereographic formula and infinity chart are verified inside the polynomial example.

contents.name: Exercises 1.3.1–1.3.3
contents.support: Bijectivity, polar-coordinate formula and agreement with the Euclidean topology justify the elementary sphere model used in the example.

contents.name: Exercises 1.3.4–1.3.8
contents.support: Finite and infinite limits and the inversion chart specify precisely the continuity checks at infinity.

contents.name: Lemma 5.1.1; Definition 5.1.2
contents.support: The polynomial specialization follows by repeated polynomial division; multiplicity is the exponent of the first nonzero factor, and the remaining factor stays nonzero on a small disk.

sources.read_evidence: Full 304-page PDF fetched. scope_notes: Hatcher chapter files and full edition are one treatment, not independent sources. May and Miller are independent full treatments. Read ranges are explicit and disjoint. Adapted mathematical lemmas are tagged ai-altered and have concrete proof obligations in pages.json and notes.md.
